title: Manual leading './' stripping loop is subsumed by posixpath.normpath
description: In _normalize_repo_path, the `while path.startswith("./"): path = path[2:]` loop preceding `posixpath.normpath(path)` is redundant. posixpath.normpath already collapses any number of leading './' (and '//') segments: normpath('./src/x.py') == 'src/x.py', normpath('././/src/x.py') == 'src/x.py'. The only adjacent case is a path like './../x.py': the loop reduces it to '../x.py', which normpath keeps and the subsequent `normalized.startswith('../')` guard then rejects with CriticalCoverageError; without the loop, normpath('./../x.py') is directly '../x.py' and trips the exact same guard. Removing the two-line loop (and keeping just the strip()+normpath+guard) preserves behavior on all inputs.
evidence: Line 53: `path = raw_path.replace("\\", "/").strip()`; Lines 54-55: `while path.startswith("./"): path = path[2:]`; Line 56: `normalized = posixpath.normpath(path)`. posixpath.normpath collapses leading './' and '//' itself, so the loop never changes the final `normalized` value nor the './..' guard outcome.
behavior_preservation: Identical: normpath subsumes leading './' collapsing for every input; the './..' edge still trips the same startswith('../') guard with or without the loop.
